items.name: Cobranza
items.tagline: Billing and reconciliation for a nonprofit therapy foundation.
items.problem: The foundation tracked payments in spreadsheets, and keeping them in order had become unmanageable.
items.how: I took over an unfinished prototype and rebuilt it. The billing logic (late fees, quarterly discounts, session packages and bank-transfer reconciliation) lives in tested functions. Auth.js separates the Admin, Staff and Accounting roles, and a test fails if any server action lacks declared permissions. A monthly cron job generates the charges.
items.result: In internal testing; the foundation is expected to start using it in December 2026. Before launch, an audit with 78 attack tests found 14 vulnerabilities, all fixed.

items.name: Donativos Bomberos Todos Santos
items.tagline: Bilingual donation platform for the volunteer fire department of my hometown.
items.problem: The fire department needed a way to receive donations online.
items.how: Stripe Elements with PaymentIntent for one-time and recurring donations in MXN, using signed webhooks and idempotent handling so records are never duplicated. Supabase PostgreSQL schema, an admin panel protected by Next.js middleware, and Spanish/English routes with next-intl. I scoped and prioritized features directly with the department's leadership.
items.result: Finished and deployed to a test environment; launch is waiting on legal paperwork with the department.

items.name: KueskiPay Credit Widget
items.tagline: Chrome extension that surfaces buy-now-pay-later credit inside the store.
items.problem: A Kueski challenge at Tec: show credit options right at the moment of purchase.
items.how: Manifest V3 extension with a React 19 popup and content scripts that detect product and price on live retail pages. A 5-table Supabase schema with Row Level Security isolates each user's credit data and purchase history. An installment calculator adapts the plan to the credit score, and a price comparator checks several stores.
items.result: Working prototype built for the challenge.
